tei:summary.tei:seg: Benjamin Satterthwaite was an English Quaker, the first of Thomas Satterthwaite and Mary Ledger’s three children. Born in Leeds in 1718, he moved to Lancaster in 1731 with his mother and siblings following the death of his father in 1728. Benjamin spent the majority of his life serving as resident factor in the West indies for his family’s firm and documented his time as factor in the form of a letter book comprised of three volumes. The letters in the third volume were written by his son John Satterthwaite. John worked as a factor in the West Indies in the 1770s.

The first volume follows Benjamin’s life as factor in Barbados for the Townson-Rawlinson-Dilworth family firms from 1737 to 1741. In 1741 Benjamin marries Anglican-born Jane Casson and is subsequently disowned by his family and the Society of Friends for a brief period.

Letter
Cork August th e 18th 1737
Honoured father
When we saild from Peele I was not
willing to write being not very Certain of the time of our
Sailing but Desired M iste r Winter to acquaint thee as soon
as he found we were sail'd which I hope he Did, we arriv ed
here the 6th Instant and that day went up to Hoare & Pike
and got the Horses landed that day which was in good
order considering but I believe they don't give the Conte
expected, there was not Beef to be got neither new
nor old so consulted w i th Hoare & Pike whether they
thought proper the ship sho'd be detain'd untill
they could make up the Quantity a Beef thou orderd
but they did not think it proper being they could
not get it in any reasonable time & it being
@ 26 / p er Barrel they thought thou wo'd not be well plea sed
with it, so ventred to take 50 firkins butter in the room
of it more then what was order'd, we are now ready to
saile but no great signes of a favourable wind
but if the weather be any thing moderate expects to
sail tomorrow let the wind be where it will our
Capt ain was very much troubled when he found' there was
no Beef to be got so soon as he expected but has lost no
time the wind blown fresh westerly euer since we arriv'd
the amount of butter on thine & Go. Acco un t is Irish £201.11.5
and on G acco un t £15.4.11 wishing the & all friends well
is the present needfull save Duty to Mo ther & love to
Bro the rs & Sisters from thy Dutifull & obedient Son
Benja min . Satterthwaite

Letter
Barbado's Novem be r 7th 1737
Dear Mother,
We arrived here the 13th Ult im o after 55 days
passage where we found Abra in good health, we sail'd from
Cork
th e 20th Aug u st
ab ou t 8 in the Morning w i th the wind @ NW blowing very
hard but after that had very pleasent weather, have had my
health very well ever since I left home this Island is now very
healthy & expects a good Crop, we are Come to a pretty good Markett
for provisions Butter @ 8/2d single, @ 7d p er quantity, Candles @ 9d-
single, @ 7 1/2d p er quantity, Cheese 6 @ 8d p er ll Dry goods goes of
slow but @ a middleing price, Capt ai n Wayles saild from this
place the Day before we arrived, am afraid thou wa'd make
thy self uneasy when thou hear'd we was not arrived, sho'd
have write the from Cork but having no opportunity but
by the post & thou being gone to Leeds thought one Letter wo'd
serve & hopes thou Did not take it a miss. I having had my
health so well ever since I left home hath encourag'd me to
stay behind the Vessall w hi ch hopes will be of servis both to my
self & Abra & shall behave my self so that it will be a pleasu re
& comfort both to thee & father which is the Desire of thy Dutiful
Son
Ben jamin Satterthwaite
P. S Please to give my kind Love to Brot her s Sisters & peggy &
accept th e same thy self - BS
P er the Jane Sam ue l Sandys
for Lancaster

Letter
Barbado's Novem be r 7th 1737
Dear Bro the r,
This will advise thee of our arrivall here th e
13th Ult im o after 55 days passage we saild from Cork the 20 August
ab ou t 8 in the morning under Double Reeft Topsails w i th wind at
NW but when we came abrest oth old head was obliged to
hand them w i th a very stiff gale & a great sea w hi ch made me
sick it Did but continue 2 Days but was squamich near a week
after that had fine weather till we Expected to make th e Land
of Barbado's & then had very Squally weather w i th prodigious
shours Rain thunder & Lightning I wish my father may
send
& enter in Butter or Candles, or part of both had
13 Cheeses & 20 firkins butter w i th me on that Acco un t w hi ch will
turn out to advantage Butter 7d @ 8 1/2d p er ll all sold, Cheese
6d @ 9d p er 2/3 sold sha'd have remitted some thing in the Jane
but as we expect a good crop the Next Year, thought it
wa'd be better to Drive it till then Sugars being Now
so very Dear, Yesterday Abra Rec eive d 2 letters from Alderm an
Jo h n Casson, advising Van Camp was very bad @ Jam aic a
but hopes he is safe arrived w i th you some time ago
here w i th have sent thee 4 bottles choice Rum w hi ch please
to accept off from- thy Loving Brother-
Benja min Satterthwaite
P er the Jane Sam ue l Sandys
for Lancaster

Letter
Barbados Novem be r 7th 1737
Ja me s Backhouse
Respected Fr ien d
This will advise you of our arrivall
here the 13th Ult im o after a long but a pleasent passage herew i th
have sent Mrs Backhouse one pott of sugar (these being no barr e ls
to be had) Returns for part of her venture was obliged to bring
all the Cheese into an Average, because we could see no marks
on them, we have not sold them all so y e t Does not know what
her sales will amount too, the frist ship that comes here will
come too a good market for provisions. Beef being Now @ 45/p er b b arre l
Butter 7d @ 8½d p er ll Candles 7½ @ 9d p er Cheese 6 @ 7 ½d p er ll Dry
goods goes of very slow but at a middling price, we expect a
very good crop of sugar here th e Next year but am afraid it will
be very Dear, w hi ch is all at present from
yo u r assured fr ien d & Serv an t to Command
Benja min Satterthwaite
IB.. 1 pott sugar.
q uanti ty 52 @ 5/2 d per £1.3.10
Whilst I was at peele I winded up th e Watch one forenoon
ab ou t 10 a Clock & it went untill five & then stood, was afraid
of writing to you ab ou t it, but when we got to Cork, got a new
Spring put into it (the other being broak w hi ch cost 6/6 Irish
has not yet sold it but shall pay you for it when I come home
w hi ch I hope will be the first Next Crop – B.. S
P er the Jane San ue l Sandys
for Lancaster

Letter
Barbados Nov 19th 1737
Dear Father
Mine to mother on 7th Ulto Instant wo’d
Wo’d advise my arrival here to a tolerable market for provision
w hi ch is Now all sold, as I have many times observed by letter
from Barbados whilst I was at home that provisions
commonly bare a good price ab ou t this time a year, encouraged
me to take 50 firkins more then was order’d being there was
no Beef to be had, the Butter and cheese on acco un t. I will turn
out to great advantage cannot yet tell what the sales
will amo un t too, and for returns shall follow thy Directions
there is no VeSsale arrived here since Sandy’s saild,
ff yr Industry comes here first VeSsale w i th new Beef
will do very well it being now 45/lb 6 bl as to yr prices
of good here Refires the i ntirely to Prabra he having so yet
thee pretty fully ther of shall do my endeavour to promote
the Intrest . I am come ab ou t so hopes Abra will have nothing
to acquaint you w i th but my good behaviour to him w hi ch
is y ou r present. Needful save dear love to Mother Brother and
sisters Peggy and all Inquiring fr ien ds. Please to accept y ou r same
thy self from – my dutifull and obedient son
Benja min Satterthwaite
P.S. I believe shall not have another opportunity of writ in g
The file next crop, have writ to Bro the r Tom enclos e d in a letter
To Mr Touchet B.S.
Capt Fallon s
For London

Letter
Barbados Nov 19th 1737
Dear Bro the r
This will advise y ou of my arrival here yr 13 Ult o
after a long passage had very fine weather till we expected
to make yr land of Barbados and then had very squally weather
w i th great rain thunder and lightning the mate and me made
land ab ou t in the morning bearing west /4 N distance
4 leagues, the veSsale that Jeame in Saild hence ab ou t 9 days
Ago sho’d have com’d home on her but having had my health
So very well thought it wo’d be better for me to stay till next crop.
I wo’d not have thee to think of going to Lancaster till I arrive
There w hi ch hope will be the latter end of June or yr foreend of
July next, but however as soon as I arrive shall advise thee
Thereof wishing thee health and liking is yr present needful
From thy loving Bro the r
Benja min Satterthwaite
Capt Fallows
For London

Letter
Barbado’s Janu a ry 29th 1737
Honoured father
I wrote thee p er Capt Fallow’s who saild hence
the 3rd Decem be r & is put into Antigua by springing a Leak so
thought it my Duty to advise thee how we proceeded, have only
sold
most part of th e
ab ou t £1720 on
BI Acc oun t both
the p Industry & ann & Bettys cargo
the marketts here are now very bad Common ¾ is sold @ 10d @ 10 ½d @ 11d p er y ar d
& Dutch Chk @ 20 @ 21d p er y ar d & goes of very slow also cutllary is ameer
Drugg – Abra will advise of his Buying a sloop
in co mpany w i th H enry Serjeant
on BI Co.
Acc oun t
w hi ch saild for th e Leward Islands the 23 rd Curr en t w i th
the
of £700 in cash & goods but doth not expect her up again before
the Industry leaves this place
w hi ch
I intend to take my passag
in w i thout I receive orders to the contrary from thee, if the Dry season
continues shall
not have as good a crop as expect
I believe leave this place the latter end of March
& I believe shall have as much cotton Ready as she
can take in for Abra has engaged a Man in this Island
to pick up all th e cotton he can & he will supply him w i th
Money & Baggs likewise a sloop that is gone Down to
Leward Sum time ago w hi ch we expect up the latter end
Feb. or foreend March I hope the Jane who saild hence th e 8th Nov embe r
is arrived w i th you some time ago, shall not have so good a crop as was expect by Reason of the dry season Abra Received a Letter
from Capt ain Jackson advising his settling at Antigua
but to poor Marketts, he has sent us a cask containing
Handek erchief es & figured caps, Abra had just before sent
him 2 cask conta ining 360 doz en figured caps to Capt. Jackson but as
they wa’d give nothing there he order’d them Directly to
Jam aic a Consign’d Peter Woodhouse, w hi ch is all at present
save Duty to mother & love to Brot the rs Sisters & Peggy please
to accept the same thy self from-
thy Dutifull & obedient son
Benja min Satterthwaite
P er the Prince Frederick
for London

Letter
Cork Septem be r 18th 1739
Dear Uncle
I write Father Last post who wo’d advise thee of our
arrivall here on th e 14th Instant also the prices of provisions & that we
we had not found thy orders, but yesterday Capt ain Sandys went on board
& found it amongst th e Barbado’s Letters wherin thou orders 40 firkins
Butter w hi ch will be ship’t to morrow, I hope we shall be ready to
sail next day, the Vessall I mention’d in my fathers w hi ch is bound
for Barbado’s. I hear has got somthing to take in w hi ch will keep her
a week Longer by that time I hope we shall be along way on
our passage. Vessalls from Bristoll & Leverpool arrive here ever
day to take in provisions for Antigua and Jam aic a but none for Barba dos
nor has not been this season, so that I hope both we & th e Industry
if she be fitt’d out in a short time may meet w i th good Marketts, wish I
thee, & thine & Huttons fireside in a good state of health. Concludes
me for the many favours I have all ready received thy ever obliged Nep hew
Ben Satterthwaite

Letter
Cork Septem be r th e 1739
Mr Casson
Thinking to find some Leverpool or Whitehaven
vessals at passage or Cove when I go down is reason I
write now that it may be ready to put on board, fearing I sho’d
not have time after I get Down, this is chieffly to advise you
the prices of provisions, Beef 26/. p er B B arre l Expected to be lower next
month, pork 28/. no Herrings, Heart & flower de Luce Butter ab ou t
27/. Dipt candles 3/6. mo
d do 4/ p er doz en & that Sam ue l Pike was at
me to take in 80 firkins w hi ch sho’d have done for you sonner the n
any one in Lancas te r but we are not to take any in upon fre ight
here is a Vessall now in the river w hi ch has taken 700 firk in s But ter
in upon freight, for Barbado’s I wish he may not have missed that opportuni ty
I hope before my next Voyage something may fall out that
will beget a better understanding betwixt my Father & you
when I get to Barbado’s shall write you the state of the
markets there by first opportunity, wishing you & your good
family all health & happiness this life can afford. Conclud e
me- Your ever real Fr ien d & Serv an t
Ben jamin Satterthwa ite
PS when ever you receive any Letters from
me & Desire you wo’d keep em to your self-
please to give my servis to Betty & th e rest of
your Daughters also to my aun t
& cousin alice,
Shall be very glad to see Henr y
at B ar B a do’s,
Ile do him all th e servis I possably can, since I writ th e
above I hear there is a vessall bound for Surinam, w hi ch will tutch at
B ar B a do’s, on whom they intend to ship your Butter, she’l be ready fo r
sailing Next week-

Letter
Octob e r 14 1739
Dear Bro the r
Since I wrote the other side father is rather Better
Abra ha m Elin was married th e 3 r d of this instant thine
T. S.

Letter
Lancaster timo 1739
Invo ice of chees shipt on board th e Industry Rich ar d
Woodhouse Mas te r for Barbados on Acco un t of Margaret
Townson & Tho ma s Satterthwaite Each /a consign’d Benja min
Satterwaite . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . Vi delicet
Lancas ter 8ber 13th 1739
Dear Brother
Above is Invo ice of Chees on board
the Industry w hi ch I Desire thou wo’d Dispose of & send
us in return a little sugar & rum w hi ch I can Dispose of Better
than cotton, the presen’t times semss to be very Difficult I
wo’d have the be very care full hough thou Dose any thing w i thout
orders for it is the oppinion of mos’t people that There will
a warr at Spring, we have not sent the any Cloths p er Industry
but as the Mary & Hope will follow shortly after have refird it till
then w i th several things besides ( my father is now in a very bore state
of health & both him and me often wish’s thou had not gone
but Hopes thinks he is rather better than he has bene I wo’d
not have thee make thy self uneasy, its unpossable for us to make
forsee what will happen) I am so throng I have scarce time to
write to thee father took the Humilitys Cargo of Hemp & flax to
Dispose of which made us much thronger Capt ain Woodhouse will
advise thee what news is stiring, Ald er man Casson’s good family all
give
there servis to thee Henry Casson intends to take his
passage in the Hope, Excuse bad reiteing I am with Due respects
thy ever well wisher & loveing Bro the r
Tho ma s Satterthwaite
TS ... 21 Thick cheeses Nett 4.0.18 .... @ 19/6 £4. 1. ......
Acco un t Mary Boton
MB ... 6 Thick cheeses Nett 1.0.3 .... @ 19/6 £1. .. .......
Lancaster B

Letter
Barbado’s December 20th 1739
Dear Father
I hope this will find thee in a much better
state of Health then when I left thee home w hi ch shall be
glad to Hear, have sold all the stockings except one doz en
thred, may send if pleases 2 doz en pair of ever sort cotton stock in gs
that I had w i th me but more will not do, the threds is all too
Dear, Hutton can advise thee what sorts will do, I intend
to ship the proceeds in French cotton by the Industry &
send thee acco un t sales, I hope I have behaved myself
so as to gain his good word. I did all that ever lay in
my power for him, he’l advise thee w ha t sort of a store I
have taken, we have been very throng in settling
Huttons Acco un ts or sho’d have writ my dear mother as
also my 2 Uncle’s shall write ‘em by the Industry, Hutton
will advise thee in what manner he’s left Her cargo & w ha t
Orders, I am not to charge him any thing for shiping
nor for w ha t sugars & cotton I shall buy after he’s saild –
I desire thou wo’d write me very often that I may know
how to proceed w hi ch is the Needfull save kind love-
from thy Dutifull & obedient son
B. S-
P er the Jane
Same time writt Bro the r W illia m & sent him a small Pa rcel Limes &
a stone Bottle rum- also write Bro the r Tomey w i th a sto Bottle rum
write alderm an the state of the market-

Letter
Barbado's Janu ary th e 10th 1739/40
Dear Father
This will advise I hope this will fin'd Hutton
safe arrived sometime before this comes to hand w i th you
out of Danger of the Spaniards he left this I took his passage
in the Jane who left this the 20th Decem be r a full ship, have now
as much sugar as will Ballast the Industry, who arrived here th e
29th Ult im o have sold her cargo at much such prices as Hutton sold
the Janes at, Excepting afew Tuffts, blew grograms, Hanc erchiefs
w hi te stripes &c. & worsted caps, w hi ch have by me, but hopes to turn
them to some a good advantage, Capt ain Day came up ab ou t 4 Days after
Hutton sail'd & only bro ugh t 4000 w eigh t cotton but he intends to sail to
night w i th cash instead of goods to purchase cotton that he maybe
up the sooner, he tells me he'll be up in 3 weeks at longest, we
Dayly expect David minville up from Martinico w i th 20,000 Weight
a large q uanti ty of
cotton
If shod be Disapointed of the cotton proposes to fill her up w i th
rum as thou orders & send Her North abo u t to Belfast there to
apply to Charles Walsh for thy orders, but hopes shall not be
disapointed of th e cotton, have sold all my most provisions Beef 32/10d
Herrings 23 they provd but ordinary 40 or 50 pretty well the rest Butter 4 p er some of it prov'd
excessive bad it begun to run out of the firkins some of
w hi ch obliged me to sell at that price & to lett 'em have 20 Barr e ls
Beef
(w hi ch prov'd very good)
w i th 40 firkins or else might keep it, I advised w i th wayles
& did to the best of my Judgeme en t for the concern, them that
I sold my cargo Dry goods too, tells me their shall not be aps 3/4 sold
under 12d p er y ar d. this year, yesterday a sloop arrived from
Antigua that gave an acco un t Beef was 3 pistolls a B b arre l
there w hi ch has started provisions a little & if now upon the rise
severall people ship Provisions inv. down there, if the Dry
weather continues shall have a good crop severall mills
ab ou t th e Latter end this mo nth , none of our countrymen yet arriv'd
since the Industry who lost her boat by bad weather ab ou t
the latto 43:00 but none of her goods Damaged, on the other
side has Q uanti ty & prices of goods sold at, I begg thou wod write
me by all opportunitys that I may know how to proceed

I hope by Capt ain Serjeant or th e Mary to hear of thy better
health w hi ch is the wishes of thy Dutifull & obedience son
BS-
p er Capt ain Fell
for London

Letter
Barbado’s Janu ar y 11th 1739/40
Dear Uncle
Have writt Father the Needfull by this conveyance
to w hi ch begg leave to refer, have sold cask No. 1 & 2 on thy acco un t Ca sk
No. 2 Turns out ab ou t 90 p er Ct but thred seate
reaches 50 p er Ct. have
also sold the Bale cott on on acco un t WD at 14/ the remainder shall
Take all possabble care in the sale there of. I hope Hutton will
be arrived sometime before this comes to hand he took his
passage w i th Capt ain Sandys who left this place the 20th ult im o
yesterday Day I begun to ship sugar ab oar d the Industry, if the
cotton I mention'd in my Fathers was but com'd up cou'd get her
ready to sail by latter end Next week, candles I believe will
be a good articule this year, thou may judge by the list from
Cork of w ha t provisions has been ship'd whether they wo'd answ e r
here in the spring better then I can pretend, w hi ch is the Needfull
save kind respects to thee & thine from thy obliged nephew
Ben Satterthwaite
please to acco un t Hutton tha t last night betwixt 2 & 3
w hi t e sug a r
was stole out of the h ogs h ea d No. 33 in W Roberts store kitchin,
shall make all possable inquiry I can
he intends to make me pay sotage for the sugar & c. have
inquir'd as Hutton Desir'd one for a bill but cannot get one
they behin to expect 34 p er 6t Exchange
P er Capt ain Fell for London

Letter
Barbado's Febru ar y 29th 1739
Charles Welsh,
afore'going is Invo ice of 29 h ogs h ead ds rum ab oar d the In'dustry
w hi ch I suppose thau'l have received orders ab ou t from my Father
Miles Townson w hi ch makes anything I can say needless
the Butter that came by the Industry proved very ordinary
excepting that w hi ch had the fleuron illustration upon' em, the beef prov some of
it proved very good also the Herrings proved midling, prices of
provisions as fallows Beef 37.10 p er score Butter 5d at 6d Herring
£23/9 p er score Tallow 8d p er ll Candles wo'd give any thing but
none to be had if thou sends such a quantity of provisions
enter half for Barbado's & half for Madera & if sho'd
send any candles always enter 'em out for Madera
which is the needfull from thy assured Fr ien d
Ben Satterthwaite
p er the Industry
Letter
B ar b a dos Feb ruary 29th 1739
p er the Industry
Dear Brother
Aforegoing is Invoice of sundrys
aboard the Industry on Acc oun t G also acco un t sales and
acco un t Curr en t and inclosd bill of Loading which I wish
safe to hand & I doubt not but will please they are
the best sugars I could light on at th e pices New
Musco vado sugars is expected to break at 22/6 p er I took all
posable care in the disposall of the Industrys Cargo
if she had call'd at Cork for her Butter & Beef
it would have been a great deal in the cargo's way
because I was oblig'd to sell my beef & candles to
get the Butter of my hands some of which was
runing out of the ferkins but some prov'd tollerable
well the Mary nor any of our countrymen yet arrived
last 3rd day arrived 2 vessalls from Cork but no letters
if I had my candles now I could make a fine hand
of them I believe I could get 10d or 11d p er ll round which
is the needfull save kind repects to all inquiring friends
from thy loving Brother

Letter
Barbados Feb ruary 29th 1739
Tho ma s Hut chinson Rawlinson
Respected
Dear Father
Aforegoing is acco un t sales of th e stockins that I had w i th
me, also acco un t of 2 Baggs choice cotton, ship't on the
Industry w hi ch I wish safe to hand doubts not but will please
I writt thee the state of th e market pretty fully by
Capt ain Fell for London (w hi ch I hope is com got to hand
ear this he saild the 12th January) since w hi ch L no
alteration excepting in Beef Tallow & Candles
Beef at 42/6 p er single but expected lower goes of very
slow & is expected lower, two Cork men is just arrived w hi ch
gives an acco un t of severall vessal's wo'd be ready to
sail soon after them w i th provisions for this place
but tallow I believe
wod give 8d p er
9d p er the quantity
& candles 10d p er by the q uantit y but not to be had excepting
by a single pound wh i ch they sell at 18d p er & 2/
I have sent
the Invoice of what is on b oar d the Industry to Hutton being
an acco un t of the cash he left w i th me, he order me to
do so that he might Devide 'em on seperate acco un ts
I have writt him pretty fully the reason of the
Industrys so long stay here, w hi ch has given me a great
deal of uneasiness being the first voya ge you might judge
it was neglect, I have given capt ain Woodhouse orders
if possable to go north ab ou t & call at Belfast there to
